questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language, the academic reputation of the university, the possibility of receiving an Erasmus-scholarship.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay, they took a long time to answer questions per e-mail, and they sometimes seemed annoyed when you asked, which could have been avoided, if they provided better information from the beginning.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its a great way to get to know people outside the university.

Additional comments:

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was difficult, as they used different digital systems for application and registration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered every class I wanted, although I had to write to several professors to make it happen.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything is possible if you just take your time to write to professors or lecturers.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Courses were open both to BA and MA students, although the size of the exams differed.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At Heidelberg University the lectures differed more clearly from the seminars; lectures were in an auditorium with a one way communication, seminars in smaller classrooms with more dialogue and an expectation of more participation. The teaching was more demanding, asking more questions, cultivating a better relation with the students. In Copenhagen, the teaching mostly happens through a PowerPoint and the teachers often take no regard of whom they actually teach.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The courses change every semester, so I can't really recommend anything. I can recommend researching the different teachers and choosing your course not only on ground of the course theme, but also depending on their research area.

questions.answer: I don't really know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I participated in a local reading group, which, although perhaps academic, were a meaningful personal experience and gave me many friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The local cities and towns, the nature, hiking trips, Schwarzwald.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy as a Dane.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn the language, eat dinner in the cantine with classmates.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Germans have a high standard of cleaning and of organization in general, which, although mostly good, can sometimes be difficult.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The history, the language, the literature

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Learn the language.
Engage in the local culture.
Travel around the area.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning the language.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning the language.
